newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Hashimoto says considering renewing China grants.
newsitem.headline: Hashimoto says considering renewing China grants.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Monday he was considering lifting a freeze on grant-in-aid to China that Tokyo imposed as a sanction over Chinese nuclear tests.

"We are making our best efforts to consider renewing the grant-in-aid (to China)," Hashimoto told a news conference in Manila after attending the summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum at Subic Bay north of the capital.
"President Jiang and I were able to have very constructive talks and I am sure President Jiang feels the same," Hashimoto added.

Hashimoto told Jiang in a meeting on the APEC sidelines on Sunday that he would strive to prevent an escalation of an islands dispute and said he would uphold a World War Two government apology issued by the Japanese government last year.

The dispute over the islands, called the Senkakus in Japanese and the Diaoyus in Chinese, and Hashimoto's controversial visit to a Tokyo war shrine had severely damaged bilateral ties. Taiwan also claims the islands in the East China Sea.
The freeze on the grant-in-aid, worth $63 million, remains an obstacle to improving ties. China signed a global ban on nuclear tests in September, after conducting two nuclear tests.
The freeze was a mainly symbolic protest as Japan's programme of low-interest yen loans, which make up the bulk of its aid to Beijing, was unaffected.
Before the Jiang-Hashimoto meeting, bilateral ties were described by senior Japanese Foreign Ministry officials as being the worst since diplomatic relations were normalised in 1972.
Jiang and Hashimoto invited each other to visit their capitals, but there was no timeframe for either visit.
